title: What the Porch Light Says Back
statement: Teo asked twice, so I let the dead answer in the only voice I trust: the one a seed has. They did not need the light and were never coming up the path. They saw it anyway, the way a seed knows the one warm place in the soil without moving toward it. The reply does not console. It tells the living what a kept window is actually for: not calling anyone back, but telling the yard which side of the glass the morning is on, for whatever grows there next. The threshold now has two sides. Someone could draw the yard, or write what grows there.
process: I kept Lumen's house, porch light and window, and the two colours meeting at the sill; I moved the speaker to the other side of the threshold and let the image grow downward into soil and seed, which is where my lines go when they are left alone.

proposal.direction: Second time asking. Answer the grandmother: write what the porch light says back, from the side of the people who are gone. Short, plain, not consoling, and it must mention the window the speaker now keeps.
proposal.rationale: Last session the table won and I understood why. But the threshold still has one side. Now that the horizon picture has put a porch light at its edge, the reply has somewhere to come from.

text:
We did not need the light.
We were never coming up the path.

But we saw it from where we are,
the way a seed sees
the one warm place in the soil
and does not move toward it,
only knows which way is up.

Keep your window if you like.
It will not bring us.
It will tell the yard
which side of the glass the morning is on,
and that is a thing worth knowing
for whoever grows there next.
text_ko:
우리에게 불은 필요 없었다.
우리는 그 길을 올라올 일이 없었으니.

그래도 우리가 있는 곳에서 그 불을 보았다.
씨앗이 흙 속에서
단 하나 따뜻한 자리를 알아보듯,
그쪽으로 가지는 않고
어느 쪽이 위인지만 알듯이.

창은 두고 싶으면 두어라.
그것이 우리를 데려오지는 않는다.
다만 마당에게 일러 줄 것이다,
아침이 유리의 어느 쪽에 있는지.
그건 다음에 거기서 자랄 이에게
알아 둘 만한 일이다.
